LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 12.1.1 LISTENING AND OBSERVING RESPOND: VIEWS/ OPINIONS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.1: Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 12.1.1 Listening and Observing Respond: Views/ Opinions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 12.1.1 Listening and Observing Respond: Views/ Opinions, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How are opinions expressed? 2. Why is it important to express one’s opinion? 3. How can expressing opinions/views affect relationships?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 12.1.1 Listening and Observing Respond: Views/ Opinions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Learners reflect on their own work as they discuss various views/opinions.

● Digital literacy: Learners interact with digital technology when searching online and listening or observing an oral narrative from

digital gadgets.

Values:
● Respect: Learners understand and appreciate others expressing opinions during group activities.

● Unity: is inculcated as learners take turns in activities and engaging in group work.

Link to other Subjects

The learner is able to relate the observing and listening skills to their learning in Kiswahili or Kenya Sign Language
